subject: literature
passage: Whenever the family asked Uncle Matthias to play at a wedding, he gave the same answer: he had sold his violin thirty years ago and had long since forgotten every note. Sofia had always believed him. But on the afternoon she helped him clear out his workshop, she noticed that the fingertips of his left hand were hard and ridged, as a violinist's become from pressing down strings, and that the sleeve of his good coat was dusted with a fine pale powder, like the rosin her own teacher rubbed onto his bow before every lesson. She said nothing, but she began to suspect that her uncle ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: had never actually learned to play the violin when he was young.
choices.B: hoped that Sofia would ask her teacher to give him lessons.
choices.C: had bought back the very violin he sold thirty years ago.
choices.D: still played the violin, despite what he told the family.

explanation.why: Two clues point the same way. Hardened fingertips on the left hand come from pressing violin strings, and the powder on his sleeve looks like rosin used on a bow. Both suggest recent playing, which contradicts his claim to have forgotten the violin.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The clues suggest the opposite: his fingertips and sleeve show signs of a practiced player, not someone who never learned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests that Matthias wants lessons from Sofia's teacher.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The clues suggest he plays a violin, but not that it is the same one he sold; he could have any instrument.
explanation.D: Correct. Fingertips hardened by strings and rosin dust on his sleeve both suggest that he still plays, though he tells the family otherwise.
